name: Regulated stablecoin payment rails
summary: Regulated fiat-backed stablecoin infrastructure moves redeemable digital money between wallets and financial institutions, especially for settlement and cross-border business payments.
useCase: A business pays an overseas supplier through a service that converts bank money to a compliant stablecoin, transfers it, and converts it into the supplier’s local bank balance.
whyNow: USDC circulation provides a transparent issuer proxy: it contracted between 2022 and 2023, then rose to $43.857 billion at end-2024 and $75.266 billion at end-2025. Circle reported $73.3 billion at the end of June 2026, below the previous year-end despite 19% growth over the same quarter a year earlier. This non-linear history matters. Circulation includes trading, savings and financial-market uses as well as payments, so it is not a retail-payments measure. Fiserv’s October 2026 launch of digital-asset infrastructure shows established financial-service suppliers entering production. Useful adoption depends on reliable redemption, compliant entry and exit, and a better total customer experience.

mainstream.scope: Routine stablecoin-based settlement, cross-border B2B transfers and selected treasury workflows through regulated service providers; not all domestic consumer payments.
mainstream.rationale: Existing circulation and payment-provider integration reduce infrastructure risk. Businesses can adopt through intermediaries without managing wallets directly, but banking access, redemption liquidity, regulation and local payout coverage determine real usefulness. Strong domestic instant-payment systems can remain competitive. The date is a selected-workflow estimate, not a claim that stablecoins replace bank deposits.

metric.name: USDC in circulation
metric.scope: Circle-issued USDC outstanding; one issuer and all uses, not payment volume.
metric.limitations: 2022–2025 are year-end stocks; the 2026 point is June 30. Do not label it full-year 2026 or compare mismatched periods as annual growth. Supply is not real-economy payment throughput. Onchain volume includes trading, transfers and potentially repeated movement of the same funds.
metric.futureNote: No defensible comparable external deployment forecast found. The separate maturity path is an analyst scenario, not measured adoption.

milestones.text: Stablecoins were already used in digital-asset markets; no directly comparable year-end issuer value retained from the selected filings.
USDC year-end circulation was $44.554 billion in Circle’s prospectus comparison.
Year-end USDC circulation fell to $24.412 billion, demonstrating that the market does not grow in a straight line.
USDC year-end circulation recovered to $43.857 billion.
USDC reached $75.266 billion at year-end; Circle’s public listing makes issuer economics more transparent.
Circle reported $73.3 billion at June quarter-end. Fiserv announced its digital-asset platform was live on 1 October; neither event establishes total global payment penetration.

tailwinds: Continuous settlement can help businesses that operate across time zones.
Established payment and banking providers can hide technical complexity from customers.
Clear reserve, redemption and compliance frameworks can improve institutional confidence.
bottlenecks: The complete path includes FX, local banking, compliance and payout costs, not only a blockchain fee.
Reserve management, redemption access and operational resilience are fundamental.
Customer protection, wallet security and regulatory treatment differ across jurisdictions.
watchMetrics: Adjusted real-economy payment volume, unique paying businesses and repeat use.
End-to-end cost, settlement time and failed-payment rates for a specific corridor.
Reserve quality, redemption latency, issuer concentration and dependence on interest income.
